chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Ash'ari from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd Allah from his father who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the marriage of women who have been triple-divorced, so he said to me, 'Indeed, your divorce is not permissible for others [to remarry them], and their divorce is permissible for you because you do not consider the triple divorce [to be final], while they consider it final.' So if it is said, 'How is this statement possible for you in light of what has been narrated:'

key_terms.طَلَاقَكُمْ: Your divorce (referring to the Shia practice)

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on triple divorce and how does it differ from other schools?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) elucidates the principle of *al-ṭalāq lahum wa-lā lanā* (divorce is for them, not for us), explaining that because Shias view a simultaneous triple divorce as revocable rather than final, the ex-wife remains permissible for others to marry. This contrasts with schools like the Hanafis, who consider it irrevocable, thereby prohibiting remarriage to others until a *ḥalāl* marriage occurs. The narration highlights the practical legal consequence of differing interpretations of *ṭalāq al-mughallazah* on the status of the wife in the broader community.
